The **lion** (***Panthera leo***) is a large [cat](Felidae "Felidae") of the genus *<Panthera>* native to Africa and India. It has a muscular, broad-chested body; short, rounded head; round ears; and a hairy tuft at the end of its tail. It is [sexually dimorphic](Sexually_dimorphic "Sexually dimorphic"); adult male lions are larger than females and have a prominent mane. It is a [social species](Social_species "Social species"), forming groups called prides. A lion's pride consists of a few adult males, related females, and cubs. Groups of female lions usually hunt together, preying mostly on large [ungulates](Ungulate "Ungulate"). The lion is an [apex](Apex_predator "Apex predator") and [keystone predator](Keystone_predator "Keystone predator"); although some lions scavenge when opportunities occur and have been known to hunt [humans](Human "Human"), lions typically do not actively seek out and prey on humans.

The lion inhabits [grasslands](Grassland "Grassland"), [savannahs](Savannah "Savannah") and [shrublands](Shrubland "Shrubland"). It is usually more [diurnal](Diurnality "Diurnality") than other wild cats, but when persecuted, it adapts to being active [at night](Nocturnality "Nocturnality") and [at twilight](Crepuscular "Crepuscular"). During the <Neolithic> period, the lion ranged throughout Africa and Eurasia from Southeast Europe to India, but it has been reduced to fragmented populations in [sub-Saharan Africa](Sub-Saharan_Africa "Sub-Saharan Africa") and one population in [western India](Western_India "Western India"). It has been listed as [Vulnerable](Vulnerable_species "Vulnerable species") on the [IUCN Red List](IUCN_Red_List "IUCN Red List") since 1996 because populations in African countries have declined by about 43% since the early 1990s. Lion populations are untenable outside designated protected areas. Although the cause of the decline is not fully understood, [habitat loss](Habitat_loss "Habitat loss") and conflicts with humans are the greatest causes for concern.

One of the most widely recognised animal symbols in human culture, the lion has been extensively depicted in sculptures and paintings, on national flags, and in contemporary films and literature. Lions have been kept in [menageries](Menagerie "Menagerie") since the time of the [Roman Empire](Roman_Empire "Roman Empire") and have been a key species sought for exhibition in [zoological gardens](Zoological_garden "Zoological garden") across the world since the late 18th century. [Cultural depictions of lions](Cultural_depictions_of_lions "Cultural depictions of lions") were prominent in [Ancient Egypt](Ancient_Egypt "Ancient Egypt"), and depictions have occurred in virtually all ancient and medieval cultures in the lion's historic and current range.

Reaching a maximum confirmed length of 29.9 meters (98 ft) and weighing up to 199 tonnes (196 long tons; 219 short tons), it is the [largest animal known ever to have existed](Largest_and_heaviest_animals "Largest and heaviest animals").[[lower-alpha 1]](Blue_whale#cite_note-5) The blue whale's long and slender body can be of various shades of greyish-blue dorsally and somewhat lighter underneath. There is also a population in the waters off Chile that may constitute a fifth subspecies.

In general, blue whale populations migrate between their summer feeding areas near the poles and their winter breeding grounds near the tropics. Blue whales are [filter feeders](Filter_feeder "Filter feeder"); their diet consists almost exclusively of [krill](Krill "Krill"). They are generally solitary or gather in small groups, and have no well-defined social structure other than mother-calf bonds. The [fundamental frequency](Fundamental_frequency "Fundamental frequency") for blue whale vocalizations ranges from 8 to 25 Hz and the production of vocalizations may vary by region, season, behavior, and time of day. ## Conservation Status Summary

| Species | Conservation Status | Endangered? |
|---------|-------------------|-------------|
| **Blue Whale** | **Endangered** | ✅ Yes |

**Blue Whale** - ✅ **Endangered**
- Listed as Endangered by IUCN
- Was hunted almost to extinction by whalers until the ban in 1966
- Still faces threats from ship strikes, pollution, and climate change

**Fin Whale** - ⚠️ **Vulnerable** (not endangered)
- Second-longest cetacean after the blue whale
- Was heavily hunted during the 20th century (over 725,000 taken from Southern Hemisphere alone)
- Population still recovering but at high risk of extinction

- Main threats: habitat loss and human-wildlife conflict

- Listed as Near Threatened since 2002
- Wild population is declining due to habitat loss, fragmentation, and poaching
- Not currently endangered, but close to qualifying for threatened status

Only the **blue whale** is officially classified as "Endangered" among these five species.
